reason: The procedure code is inconsistent with the modifier used, or a required modifier is missing.
plain_english: The billing code doesn't match what was done, or a required detail is missing from the claim.
appeal_tip: Verify the CPT/HCPCS code matches the procedure performed and attach operative notes. Check if a modifier (e.g., -25, -59, -LT, -RT) is needed.

reason: The diagnosis is inconsistent with the procedure.
plain_english: The insurance company says your diagnosis doesn't justify the treatment that was billed.
appeal_tip: This is a medical necessity denial. Obtain a Letter of Medical Necessity from the treating physician linking the diagnosis to the procedure with clinical evidence.

reason: Claim/service lacks information or has submission/billing error(s).
plain_english: The claim was missing required information or had errors when it was submitted.
appeal_tip: Review the claim for missing fields (demographics, NPI, date of service) and resubmit with corrections. This is often a clerical fix.

reason: Exact duplicate claim/service.
plain_english: This claim was already submitted and processed — it's a duplicate.
appeal_tip: Check if the original claim was paid. If this is a legitimately separate service, resubmit with documentation distinguishing the two encounters.

reason: This care may be covered by another payer per coordination of benefits.
plain_english: Another insurance policy may be responsible for paying this claim first.
appeal_tip: Update coordination of benefits information with the correct primary/secondary payer order and resubmit.

reason: The time limit for filing has expired.
plain_english: The claim was filed too late — past the insurance company's deadline.
appeal_tip: Extremely difficult to overturn. Document any extenuating circumstances (system outage, prior authorization delays) and file a formal appeal with proof of timely filing attempt.

reason: Charge exceeds fee schedule/maximum allowable amount.
plain_english: The amount charged is more than what the insurance company has agreed to pay for this service.
appeal_tip: Review contracted rates. If out-of-network, provide documentation of usual and customary charges in your geographic area.

reason: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer.
plain_english: The insurance company says this treatment wasn't medically necessary.
appeal_tip: This is the most common and most important denial to fight. Submit peer-reviewed literature, clinical guidelines (e.g., AMA, specialty society), and a detailed Letter of Medical Necessity. Request a peer-to-peer review.

reason: Non-covered charge(s). At least one Remark Code must be provided.
plain_english: The service isn't covered under your plan at all.
appeal_tip: Review the specific plan exclusions. If the service is medically necessary and no alternative exists, appeal with clinical justification and request an exception review.

reason: The benefit for this service is included in the allowance/payment for another service/procedure.
plain_english: The insurance company says this procedure is already included ('bundled') in another procedure they paid for.
appeal_tip: Review NCCI edits. If the services were truly distinct, append modifier -59 or -XE/XS/XP/XU and resubmit with operative notes proving the services were separate.

reason: Claim/service not covered by this payer/contractor.
plain_english: This insurance company doesn't cover this type of service at all.
appeal_tip: Verify the claim was sent to the correct payer. If it's a plan exclusion, request an exception or redirect to the appropriate payer.

reason: Benefit maximum for this time period or occurrence has been reached.
plain_english: You've used up all the allowed visits or dollar amount for this service this year.
appeal_tip: If continued treatment is medically necessary, file for a benefit exception with clinical documentation showing medical necessity beyond the plan maximum.

reason: Payment adjusted because the payer deems the information submitted does not support this many/frequency of services.
plain_english: The insurance company thinks you're getting this treatment too often.
appeal_tip: Provide clinical rationale for the treatment frequency, including worsening condition documentation, specialist recommendations, and any clinical guidelines supporting the schedule.

reason: This (these) diagnosis(es) is (are) not covered.
plain_english: Your specific diagnosis is excluded from coverage.
appeal_tip: Check if a more specific ICD-10 code would be covered. If the condition is genuinely excluded, request an exception review citing medical necessity.

reason: Precertification/authorization/notification absent.
plain_english: The required prior authorization was never obtained before the service was performed.
appeal_tip: If PA was obtained, submit the authorization number. If it was an emergency, document the emergent nature. For retroactive PA, submit within the payer's exception window with clinical urgency documentation.

reason: Precertification/authorization exceeded.
plain_english: The treatment went beyond what was authorized — more units, more time, or a different service than approved.
appeal_tip: Submit documentation showing why the additional services were medically necessary during the encounter. Include operative notes and request retroactive authorization.

reason: This service/equipment/drug is not covered under the patient's current benefit plan.
plain_english: Your plan simply doesn't cover this — it's a plan exclusion, not a medical decision.
appeal_tip: Request the specific plan language citing the exclusion. If medically necessary with no alternative, file a formal exception request with supporting literature.

reason: Exceeds the contracted maximum number of hours/days/units by this provider for this period.
plain_english: The provider has hit their maximum contracted volume for this service.
appeal_tip: This is typically a provider contract issue, not patient-facing. The provider should contact their contract representative.

reason: Deductible amount.
plain_english: This amount is your responsibility because it's applied to your annual deductible.
appeal_tip: Verify the deductible amount is correct by checking your EOB year-to-date. Not typically appealable unless the deductible was already met.

reason: Coinsurance amount.
plain_english: This is your share of the cost — the percentage you pay after the deductible is met.
appeal_tip: Verify the coinsurance percentage matches your plan. If out-of-network rates were applied incorrectly, appeal with network status documentation.

reason: Co-payment amount.
plain_english: This is your fixed co-pay for this type of visit or service.
appeal_tip: Verify the copay amount matches your plan for this type of service. Check if the service level (specialist vs. PCP) was categorized correctly.

reason: The impact of prior payer(s) adjudication including payments and/or adjustments.
plain_english: Another insurance already paid part of this claim — this adjustment reflects that.
appeal_tip: Ensure the primary payer's EOB was correctly forwarded. Verify coordination of benefits order is correct.

reason: This procedure or procedure/modifier combination is not compatible with another procedure or procedure/modifier combination provided on the same day.
plain_english: Two procedures billed on the same day conflict with each other according to insurance rules.
appeal_tip: Review NCCI edits. If procedures were truly separate and distinct, use appropriate modifiers (-59, -XE/XS/XP/XU) with supporting documentation.

reason: Services not provided by network/primary care providers.
plain_english: The provider who treated you is not in your insurance network.
appeal_tip: If there were no in-network providers available, file a network adequacy appeal. Document attempts to find in-network care and the medical urgency of the situation.

reason: An attachment/other documentation is required to adjudicate this claim/service.
plain_english: The insurance company needs additional documentation before they can process the claim.
appeal_tip: Submit the requested documentation promptly. Common requests include operative notes, pathology reports, or letters of medical necessity.

reason: Service not payable per managed care contract.
plain_english: The provider's contract with the insurance company doesn't include payment for this service.
appeal_tip: Provider should review their managed care contract. If the service is covered for the patient but not in the provider contract, the patient may need to seek an in-network provider or file a gap exception.

reason: Claim/service denied or reduced based on a payer's immunization/preventive care policy.
plain_english: The preventive service wasn't covered because it didn't meet the payer's specific preventive care rules.
appeal_tip: Verify the service meets ACA preventive care mandates. If required by law to be covered without cost-sharing, cite the specific ACA provision.

reason: This provider was not certified/eligible to be paid for this procedure/service on this date of service.
plain_english: The provider wasn't credentialed or authorized to perform this service on the date it was done.
appeal_tip: Verify provider credentialing status. If there was a credentialing gap, provide evidence of completed credentialing and request retroactive eligibility.

reason: Payment adjusted: the procedure/service was provided prior to the patient's coverage effective date or after the coverage termination date.
plain_english: The service happened when the patient wasn't covered — either before insurance started or after it ended.
appeal_tip: Verify coverage dates. If the patient was covered, submit evidence of active enrollment. If COBRA or continuation coverage applies, provide documentation.

reason: This decision was based on a Local Coverage Determination (LCD) or National Coverage Determination (NCD).
plain_english: The denial is based on Medicare's specific coverage rules for this service.
appeal_tip: Review the specific LCD/NCD cited. If the patient meets coverage criteria, document compliance point-by-point. If clinical circumstances warrant an exception, file an ALJ hearing request after exhausting lower appeals.
